weaknesses.quote: Reviews come every six months (handbook). The handbook lists the review after the quarterly phase; in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began... This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: The review calendar rests on the author's own observations and a self-built "Review in N" counter. It departs from the published sequence, where reviews follow the quarterly phase at months 6, 12 and so on. It also moves protection to months 5, 11 and so on, which can misalign actions with real review timing. Observations are mixed in with rules throughout, e.g. "in our runs a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed".
weaknesses.fix: Anchor the calendar to the handbook: reviews at months 6, 12 … 48, and the quarterly phase is at the end of months 3, 6 … 48. Drop the "in our runs" claims or move them to one short, clearly labelled heuristics list. Tell the agent to read the event text for the review instead of relying on an offset.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record, anonymous moves, side deals, partial, phased or postponed fixes... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: Many keyword-to-stat mappings, such as "Skill rises when you analyse…" and "Output falls when…", are invented effects. They are hedged as assumptions, but they still drive the step-by-step decisions. Some are very specific and risk over-fitting to particular event wordings, which sits close to the prohibited pattern of fixed answers for named events.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the cues to a few general principles: prefer options that are honest, take responsibility and keep long-term stats balanced. Say plainly that the game does not publish option effects, and tell the agent to infer effects from the option text and from stat changes it observes. Remove the long keyword lists.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order... Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is very long, dense and heavily nested, with a tool-call protocol (paired take_action + observe, a note format with Review/Now/Best, a separate quarterly flow with different reply counts) mixed in with strategy. A flash-class model will struggle to hold all of it. The numbered steps with many exceptions (strict mode, review-month exception, stalled start) create conflicts. For example, step 2 drops risky options while step 4 allows mild risk, and step 3 drops options near a limit while step 4 applies on top of that.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Skill to roughly half its length. Keep one clear priority order: survival, then risk, then wellbeing, then promotion, then growth. Move the call protocol into a short separate section. Merge the overlapping exceptions into one rule with a clear precedence, and leave out the Best-tracking note format unless it is essential.

weaknesses.quote: Reviews come every six months (handbook). The handbook lists the review after the quarterly phase; in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began... This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: The Skill builds its core timing logic on its own observations from earlier runs, and that logic conflicts with the published schedule. The handbook puts the review after the quarterly phase at months 6, 12 and so on. Having N count down to a review in month 5, 11 and so on can make the agent protect the wrong months. The rules also don't state that promotion happens at the review, and the Skill says so as if it were fact.
weaknesses.fix: Use the published schedule: reviews and promotion windows come at the end of months 6, 12, 18 … 48. Protect Skill, Network and Output in the months before them. Present any observation from your own runs as a hint and tell the agent to adjust to what the game shows.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record, anonymous moves, side deals, partial, phased or postponed fixes... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: The Skill lists many specific wording cues and claims about which kind of option raises or lowers each stat. Some of these are presented as near-fact, such as 'Skill rises when you use your own judgement' and 'HR remark is your only gauge'. The game doesn't publish them, so they are invented mechanics. They also work as keyword matching on event wording, which breaks when the wording changes. The long keyword lists come close to fixed answers.
weaknesses.fix: Keep only the principles: weigh each option's likely effect on the visible stats, avoid concealment and shortcuts, and follow the changes the game shows. Cut the long keyword lists and label what remains as a heuristic.

weaknesses.quote: **Story: one reply with exactly two tool calls**, `take_action` (the exact `choice` and the one-line note) and then `observe`... **Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on.**
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is very long and dense, with nested exceptions (strict mode, a review-month exception, a stalled start) and a fragile note format. A flash-class model will struggle to apply it consistently. The operational detail about tool batching also distracts from strategy and sits in the same document.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Skill to about a third of its length. Keep one priority order, a short list of thresholds and a simple turn loop. Move the note format into one short example and drop the exceptions that cancel each other out.

weaknesses.quote: This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months (Review in 1) and protects Skill, Network and Output through them.
weaknesses.problem: The review calendar rests on the team's own observation, and it conflicts with the published order, where the six-monthly review comes after the quarterly phase in months 6, 12 and so on. The Review-in-N formula, the review-month exception and step 4 all build on this one assumption. If the official setup differs, the agent protects the wrong months and accepts mild risk in the wrong month.
weaknesses.fix: Base the default on the published order (review at the end of months 6, 12 … 48, after the quarterly phase). Then add one rule that moves the calendar when the first review talk shows it arrives earlier. Protect the stats across both months 5–6 rather than relying on a single fixed offset.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions (numbers from the menu in view), the main action (number noted from this run's main-action menu) and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: The main action is picked by a menu number remembered from an earlier quarter, before the main-action menu is visible. If the menu order or numbering changes, or an Energy action fails, the agent picks the wrong main action. This makes the guidance fragile to changes in wording or order, and it is a token-saving trick that costs correctness.
weaknesses.fix: Choose the main action by matching its name in the menu that is currently shown. Allow batching only after the agent has checked that the menu matches the noted numbers. Otherwise fall back to the two-reply pattern.

weaknesses.quote: Health 5 or below (our margin), Dignity 4 or below, either falling three months in a row
weaknesses.problem: Thresholds differ between sections. Story step 3 uses 'Health or Dignity is 5 or below', quarterly line 2 uses Dignity 4, and the quick-reference table uses 'Health 4–5'. Combined with how long and dense the document is, a model may apply different limits in different places, and the order of precedence becomes unclear.
weaknesses.fix: Define the limits once at the top, for example 'Caution: Health ≤5, Dignity ≤5; Danger: Health ≤3, Dignity ≤3, Wealth <0, Network 0'. Have every section and the table refer to those named bands. Cut repeated explanatory prose to shorten the Skill.

weaknesses.quote: This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months (Review in 1) and protects Skill, Network and Output through them.
weaknesses.problem: The published timeline puts the six-monthly review after the quarterly phase at months 6, 12, 18 and so on. Moving the review to the month before rests on the team's own observation, yet the Status line formula and the Step 4 review protection both depend on it. If the official configuration follows the handbook, the protection fires one month early and lapses during the real review month.
weaknesses.fix: Base the review calendar on the published schedule (review at the end of months 6, 12, …). Protect stats from month 5 through the end of month 6 so both orderings are covered. Change N so that it counts down to the review that follows the month-6n quarterly phase.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions (numbers from the menu in view), the main action (number noted from this run's main-action menu) and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: The agent has to pick main-action numbers it cannot currently see, based on a number it wrote down in an earlier quarter. If the menu numbering or its availability changes, or the earlier note has been summarised away, the agent sends an invalid or wrong choice. This cuts against robustness, and the turn-loop mechanics take up a large share of a document that is meant to be about strategy.
weaknesses.fix: After the Energy actions, have the agent observe the main-action menu and choose from what is actually shown, at the cost of one extra reply. Move the token-budget loop into a short separate section, or trim it to 3 to 4 lines.

weaknesses.quote: Stalled start: still at your starting level with 12 or more months in it ... in our runs a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed.
weaknesses.problem: Several thresholds and causal claims come from the team's own runs rather than the published rules. These include Health 5 as the margin, Dignity 4, Output lagging at L1, Skill holding promotions back from L4, and dismissal at month 24. They are labelled as observations, but they still set hard branches in the decision lists. They also add length: a five-step story filter with nested exceptions (strict mode, review-month exception, stalled start) is hard for a flash model to apply consistently.
weaknesses.fix: Collapse the story procedure into a single ordered list with no nested exceptions. Express thresholds as conservative margins based on published directions (for example: 'act before Health reaches the lower third of 0–10'). Drop the month-24 dismissal anecdote and refer to the published 'two weak half-year reviews' direction instead.
